teaching_language.summary: The programme as a whole is bilingual: both majors exist in a fully English-taught version and a fully Italian-taught version, so an international applicant can complete the entire degree in English by selecting an English major. The degree is therefore IN SCOPE as an English-taught option (not italian_only).

campus: Rome, Italy (Luiss Guido Carli, Department of Business and Management; Viale Romania campus is the usual seat for Business and Management master's programmes). [uncertain] The programme page mentions Luiss facilities in Rome and Milan but does not name the specific building for this degree; the Milan mention appears to be a generic reference to Luiss facilities, not a delivery campus for this degree.

admission_type.route_name: Luiss Test (Master's admission test) - EU/Schengen students
admission_type.eligible_applicants: EU/Schengen citizens holding, or about to hold, a three-year bachelor's degree qualifying for master's enrolment in Italy
admission_type.test_or_certification: Luiss Test for master's degree programmes: psycho-aptitude / academic-competence questions in a GMAT-inspired format, taken online on the Luiss Webtesting platform. Marketing IS accessible via this route (it is NOT part of the Finance and Management exception).
admission_type.number_of_choices_allowed: Up to two master's degree courses, in order of preference, within the same subject area
admission_type.subject_area_group: Economics (Marketing sits in the Economics/Business subject-area group together with Management, Finance, Strategic Management and Amministrazione, Finanza e Controllo; the alternative group is Law / Political Science). [uncertain] The subject-area grouping is inferred from the minimum-curricular-requirements grouping rather than an explicit list on the test page.

admission_type.route_name: Direct admission with GMAT/GRE certification - EU/Schengen students
admission_type.eligible_applicants: EU/Schengen citizens holding, or about to hold, a qualifying three-year bachelor's degree and a valid GMAT or GRE score
admission_type.test_or_certification: GMAT minimum 515 out of 805, OR GRE minimum 154 out of 170 in BOTH the Verbal and the Quantitative sections. This route explicitly covers all Luiss master's degree courses EXCEPT Management and Finance, so Marketing IS eligible.
admission_type.subject_area_group: Not applicable - a single binding programme choice is made across the whole master's catalogue (except Management and Finance)

admission_type.route_name: Luiss Test (Master's admission test) - non-EU / non-Schengen students
admission_type.eligible_applicants: Non-EU / non-Schengen citizens who have completed or are completing a three-year degree qualifying them for master's enrolment in Italy; foreign qualifications subject to validity check by the Luiss Admissions Office
admission_type.test_or_certification: Same Luiss Test for master's degree programmes, run as a dedicated non-EU process
admission_type.number_of_choices_allowed: Up to two master's degree programmes in order of preference
admission_type.subject_area_group: Economics [uncertain] - same grouping assumption as the EU route

admission_type.route_name: Certified selection / admission with international qualifications - non-EU / non-Schengen students
admission_type.eligible_applicants: Non-EU / non-Schengen citizens holding the international qualifications required for entry to Luiss master's degree courses
admission_type.test_or_certification: Evaluation of academic qualifications; direct admission is granted where a valid GMAT or GRE certificate with the required minimum scores is submitted. This route explicitly excludes Finance and Management, so Marketing IS eligible. [uncertain] The 2027/2028 notice with exact scores and rounds is not yet published.

admission_type.route_name: Admission route for Luiss internal students
admission_type.test_or_certification: Dedicated Luiss-students admission test / internal procedure. [uncertain] Details for 2027/2028 not yet published; Luiss also historically grants direct access to high-GPA internal graduates.

admission_type.route_name: NOT APPLICABLE: Finance and Management special selection
admission_type.test_or_certification: Verified: the special selection page covers ONLY the Master's Degrees in Finance and Management (requiring GMAT minimum 555/805 or GRE minimum 157/170 in both sections, with the Luiss Test not valid). Marketing is NOT listed there, confirming Marketing follows the GENERAL master admission rules and the Luiss Test IS valid for it.

academic_requirements.prior_qualification: A three-year (first-level) bachelor's degree, or a foreign qualification awarded after at least 3 academic years (or 4, depending on the school system) that entitles the holder to enrol in graduate programmes in the awarding country. Professional and vocational qualifications are not accepted. The degree must be obtained by 18 November 2027 for the 2027/2028 Luiss Test route.
academic_requirements.minimum_curricular_requirements: Direct curricular eligibility for the group of master's programmes covering Management, Finance, Strategic Management, Marketing and Amministrazione, Finanza e Controllo is granted to holders of Italian degree classes L-18 (D.M. 270/04) and 17 (D.M. 509/99) - Economics and Business Management, and L-33 (D.M. 270/04) and 28 (D.M. 509/99) - Economics. Fallback for all other bachelor programmes: at least 24 university credits (ECTS) in total, already earned or still to be earned, spread across at least three of the subject areas Business, Economics, Statistics and Law.
academic_requirements.minimum_grade_or_gpa: [uncertain] No minimum grade or GPA is stated on the minimum-curricular-requirements page for Marketing. Luiss has historically granted direct access to its own graduates with a high weighted average, but no 2027/2028 threshold was found published.
academic_requirements.country_specific_rules: [uncertain] Not found in a Marketing-specific form. Luiss publishes general rules for foreign qualifications rather than a per-country minimum-grade table on the master's pages consulted.
academic_requirements.document_recognition: Depends on the awarding country: Diploma Supplement for signatories of the Lisbon Recognition Convention; Statement of Verification or Apostille for ARDI countries; Statement of Comparability (CIMEA) or Declaration of Value for all other countries. Foreign qualifications are validity-checked by the Luiss Admissions Office.
academic_requirements.compensatory_measures: [uncertain] No compensatory or bridging measures for master's entry were found published for Marketing; the ECTS fallback (24 credits across at least three subject areas, which may still be earned) effectively serves this role.

language_requirements.required_level: B2 in the language of instruction. For the English-taught majors, English at B2 or above; for the Italian-taught majors, Italian at B2 or above.
language_requirements.accepted_certificates: [uncertain] The master's admission pages consulted do not publish a per-certificate score table. Score levels commonly published by Luiss at the B2 threshold are IELTS 6.0, TOEFL iBT 78-80, Cambridge FCE grade B and Cambridge CAE grade C, but the pages where these appear relate to exchange/other Luiss programmes, so they should be treated as indicative and re-checked in the 2027/2028 admission notice due from November 2026.
language_requirements.assessed_in_test: Yes, in effect: the language route of the Luiss Test determines programme access. Taking the master's Luiss Test in English gives access to courses taught in both Italian and English; taking it in Italian gives access only to Italian-taught courses. [uncertain] Whether a separately scored English section sits inside the master's test, as opposed to the test simply being sat in English, is not stated explicitly on the pages consulted.
language_requirements.exemptions: [uncertain] No exemption list (e.g. for applicants whose prior degree was taught in English) was found published on the master's admission pages consulted.
language_requirements.italian_requirement_note: Applicants targeting the Italian-taught majors of Marketing must have Italian at B2; non-EU applicants to Italian-taught programmes are required to submit a certificate evidencing at least level B2 in Italian. The English-taught majors do not require Italian.

entry_exam_or_test.test_name: Luiss Test for Master's Degree Programmes (alternative route: GMAT or GRE as an external certification)
entry_exam_or_test.content: Psycho-aptitude and academic-competence questions in a GMAT-inspired format, assessing logical reasoning, problem solving and quantitative/mathematical skills. [uncertain] The detailed section breakdown and question count for the MASTER'S test are not published on the pages consulted; the widely cited 50 questions in 75 minutes with +1 / -0.25 / 0 scoring is documented for the Luiss bachelor's and single-cycle test and should not be assumed identical for the master's test.
entry_exam_or_test.format: Online, sat on the Luiss Webtesting platform. [uncertain] Proctoring arrangements and any on-campus option are not detailed on the pages consulted.
entry_exam_or_test.dates: 19 to 22 April 2027 (same window for the EU/Schengen and non-EU routes), for the 2027/2028 academic year
entry_exam_or_test.language_of_test: The candidate chooses Italian or English. Taking the test in ITALIAN grants access only to Italian-taught courses - which for Marketing means only the two Italian-language majors. Taking the test in ENGLISH grants access to courses taught in both Italian and English - so an English sitting is required to reach the English-taught Marketing majors, and it also keeps the Italian majors open.
entry_exam_or_test.interview: [uncertain] No interview is mentioned for the general master's routes. Luiss states elsewhere that applicants without a language certificate may be invited to an interview to verify their level of English, but this was not confirmed on the Marketing or general master's admission pages.

ENGLISH / ITALIAN MAJOR SPLIT (verified): Marketing is genuinely bilingual, not English-only. It offers FOUR majors - Marketing Strategy, Management and Communication and Marketing Analytics and Data Science - each existing in BOTH an English and an Italian version, flagged with UK/Italian flags on the programme page. The programme is therefore in scope as an English option; an applicant must sit the Luiss Test IN ENGLISH to reach the English majors. Sitting it in Italian locks the applicant to the Italian majors only.

LUISS TEST ELIGIBILITY (verified): Marketing is NOT on the Finance/Management exception list. The special-selection page names only Finance and Management, so the Luiss Test IS valid for Marketing, and the GMAT/GRE direct route explicitly covers 'all Luiss Master's degree courses, except for Management and Finance', which likewise includes Marketing.

SOURCE CONFLICT ON GMAT/GRE THRESHOLDS: the general direct-admission route requires GMAT 515 / GRE 154, while the Finance and Management special selection requires the HIGHER GMAT 555 / GRE 157. Marketing uses the general, lower thresholds.

SOURCE CONFLICT ON TUITION: the research outline assumed EUR 16,000 as the standard master's fee with EUR 18,000 for exceptions. The live Luiss pages show EUR 15,000 for Marketing (and for International Relations, Data Science and Management, and Economics, Institutions and Financial Markets) with EUR 17,000 for Management and Finance. The outline figures appear to be from an earlier fee schedule. The EUR 15,000 figure is quoted verbatim from the Marketing programme page.
